title: Political & Economic Geography
shortDescription: States, capitals, and borders on one side; resources, crops, and industry belts on the other — two different maps of the same country.
genZNote: Political geography is 'who owns this square'. Economic geography is 'what does this square actually produce'. Learn them as two separate overlays on the same map.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.body: Political Geography tests state/UT boundaries, capitals, and neighbouring countries. Economic Geography tests where key resources, crops, and industries are concentrated. Both build on the physical map (mountains, rivers, climate) covered separately — a region's economic activity is rarely random, it follows its physical geography.

sections.heading: States & Union Territories — the Basics
sections.body: India currently has 28 states and 8 Union Territories, following the 2019 reorganisation that split the former state of Jammu & Kashmir into the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Static-GK questions on this topic typically ask for a state's capital, its neighbouring states, or which country it borders (for border states).

sections.heading: India's Neighbouring Countries
bullets: Land borders: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Afghanistan (a short border via the Pakistan-administered region).
Sri Lanka and Maldives are neighbouring countries reached by sea, not land border.
Gujarat itself borders Pakistan (to the northwest, via the Rann of Kutch) and the Arabian Sea (to the west) — a locally relevant fact for a Gujarat-based exam.

rows: Deccan Plateau black-soil belt — Gujarat, Maharashtra
Assam, West Bengal (Darjeeling), and parts of South India (Nilgiris)
Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh — major coal-bearing states
Offshore western coast (Mumbai High), Gujarat, Assam

sections.heading: Major Ports
bullets: Kandla (Deendayal) Port and Mundra Port — major ports on Gujarat's coastline.
Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) — near Mumbai, one of India's busiest container ports.
Chennai Port and Visakhapatnam Port — major east-coast ports.

sections.heading: Common Traps
bullets: Confusing a land-bordering neighbour with a sea-only neighbour — Sri Lanka and Maldives do not share a land border with India.
Assuming resource distribution is uniform — coal/iron ore are concentrated in a specific eastern belt (Jharkhand-Odisha-Chhattisgarh), not spread evenly across the country.
Mixing up state capitals, especially for states that changed or have unusual capital arrangements.

sections.heading: Fast Recall Hooks
bullets: Coal-iron belt = Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh. Cotton belt = Deccan black soil = Gujarat, Maharashtra.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Political Geography covers state/UT boundaries and neighbouring countries; Economic Geography covers where key resources, crops, and industries are concentrated.
keyFacts: India has 28 states and 8 Union Territories after the 2019 J&K reorganisation.
Land borders: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar; Sri Lanka and Maldives are sea-only neighbours.
Coal and iron ore are concentrated in Jharkhand, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh.
Cotton is concentrated in the Deccan black-soil belt — Gujarat and Maharashtra.
commonConfusion: Sri Lanka and Maldives are often mistakenly listed as land-bordering neighbours — they are reached only by sea.

highYieldFacts: 28 states, 8 Union Territories is the current count following the 2019 J&K/Ladakh reorganisation.
Gujarat borders Pakistan and the Arabian Sea, and is a major cotton and petroleum region.
commonTraps: Treating Sri Lanka or Maldives as land-bordering neighbours of India.
